name: aversion
quote: That painting is ugly as sin.
description: Wanting to avoid a certain experience

variations.name: aesthetic aversion
variations.description: Something unattractive to the senses or sensibilities in purely subjective arena. For example colors you consider clashing or music from a genre you don't favor.

variations.name: mental aversion
variations.description: Something unattractive in the mental realm may invoke criticism and perhaps a desire to share it socially. For example, the recognition of a poorly-built instance of a favorite architectural style may create the desire to point out its flaws, and also support an identity as someone who's into that kind of thing.

variations.name: physical aversion
variations.description: Something unattractive in the social realm may invoke contempt. For example, an off-key singing voice.

variations.name: aversion signaling
variations.description: Sometimes we might recognize that a social group expects us to find a certain thing unappealing, which may nudge us into paying closer attention.

variations.name: remembered aversion
variations.description: Music or smells can bring back early formative memories. e.g. e.g. Maybe the smell of ketchup reminds you of an awkward accident.

commentaries.quote: Aesthetic aversion is always subjective. Someone else may appreciate the architecture, singing voice, graffiti, or clashing colors.
There are many reasons we may like or dislike something.

conditions: Something in the mental realm is perceived as being far from matching an ideal so that you don't want to experience it.
Something in the social environment is perceived as being far from matching an ideal held by one of your identities, so you don't want to experience it.
Something in the sensory environment is nearly the opposite of an ideal represented by an instinct or foundational memory, so you don't want to experience it.
